claim_ceiling: A successor route is a development research decision only. It is not a codec result, baseline win, validation result, or state-of-the-art claim.
name: text-source-structural-successor-routing-v1

ordered_rules.action: Develop WK-S1 on the retained TS-H1 demultiplex: a reversible bounded wiki-markup scanner with separate plain-text, template/tag, link/entity, title, and structural-metadata channels. Compare complete self-contained output against every practical and admitted research baseline.

Develop WK-S1 on TS-H1 as a diagnostic successor because demultiplexing exposed useful residual structure but missed final admission. The new scanner must earn the full five-percent gate rather than inheriting credit from TS-H1.

Reject framing demultiplex as the next Wikimedia base. Develop WK-P1 without the AXTS1 envelope: bounded markup-aware prediction plus a development-trained static token dictionary whose complete decoder bytes are counted once. Predeclare dictionary training and validation splits before fitting.

Develop TS-S1 on retained extension lanes: a reversible bounded lexical-role transform separating whitespace, comments, identifiers, literals, punctuation, and raw escape bytes within deterministic language/extension lanes. Count all framing and decoder state.
Develop TS-S1 on extension lanes because TS-H2 exposed useful language-homogeneity residuals but missed final admission. TS-S1 must independently clear the full five-percent gate.

Develop TS-S1 on TS-H1 demultiplex without extension lanes: reversible lexical-role channels with language identity retained only as bounded metadata. This tests token-role residuals without assuming extension grouping helped.

Reject AXTS1 structural separation as the next source-code base. Develop TS-P1 directly over canonical source bundles: a bounded mixed byte/token predictor with a development-trained counted static dictionary, preserving raw escape channels for unsupported syntax.
